justification: Changes which characters are deleted from every PDF page before rule text is extracted, for every council. A false positive deletes letters and words from served regulation; a false negative lets a sideways title's letters interleave into it.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a stacked list marker with its line's words beside it (the waverley 'To' bullets or 'o' sub-bullets, or markers 19pt from their words) is taken as a margin title and its band stripped; or the real marrickville title stops being found when body text sits 33-39pt from some of its glyphs, or when one stray word sits beside one glyph

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-09-13 on waverley DCP 2022 (448 pages) and marrickville part7-s3-sex-industry (28 pages). Before: the strip fired on 5 waverley pages (7, 129, 275, 356, 359), stacked 'To' bullets and 'o' sub-bullets whose nearest same-line word is 2.1-11.4pt away, and deleted 65-128 characters per page. 27 of 602 waverley rules had a line whose words are not in order on their PDF pages (251 of 8,191 lines). The real marrickville running title is on 12 odd pages; on page 25 its nearest word is 143.5pt away, on page 21 body text is 33.4-38.9pt from 6 of 38 glyphs. After: the strip fires on 0 waverley pages and all 12 marrickville title pages; waverley pages read identically to plain pdfplumber; re-extracted, 16 rules and 98 lines mismatch, and all 98 lines read the same in plain pdfplumber text (table cell order), none lost by our reading.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The detector assumed a contiguous stack of short alphabetic words at one x could only be a sideways title, and its comment recorded the 'To'-bullet false positive as solved by vertical contiguity. A tightly leaded list (2.4pt between lines) is contiguous too. The filter then removes every character whose x0 is in the band across the whole page, so a false detection cuts letters out of unrelated words.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds one condition to the existing detector, measured from the same word geometry it already reads; the filter, the callers and every other guard are unchanged, so a page that was correctly stripped before is stripped identically (50 characters on marrickville page 25 before and after).
pre_impl.external_source_error: A council whose margin title sits within 20pt of body text beside at least half its glyphs would no longer be stripped: its letters would interleave into rule text, which shows in review as garbled lines rather than silently missing words.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change. Rule text reaches users only through the review queue and the commit job.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Without this, rules served from affected pages read '(a) develop' for '(a) To develop' and 'appies' for 'applies' across councils, and a reviewer checking words against the PDF can miss a dropped short word. With it, a list is never stripped; the remaining risk is an unusual title layout not being stripped, which garbles visibly.

functions.name: _run_is_isolated
functions.input: The stacked glyph words of one candidate run and every word on the page.
functions.output: True when fewer than half of the run's glyphs have a word outside the run overlapping them vertically within 20pt horizontally.
functions.if_none: Words missing any geometry key are ignored; a run whose glyphs have no neighbours returns True.

functions.name: find_vertical_margin_label_band
functions.input: The pdfplumber extract_words() output for one page, each word with its text and bounding box, and optionally the page width.
functions.output: The (x0, x1) band of a running sideways title, now only when the run passes _run_is_isolated and, when the page width is given, lies within _MARGIN_LABEL_EDGE_FRACTION of a page edge.
functions.if_none: An empty list, no qualifying run, or a run with words beside most glyphs returns None.

functions.name: _strip_vertical_margin_label
functions.input: One pdfplumber page object from a council DCP PDF, before any text is extracted from it.
functions.output: The page with the detected title band's characters removed, or the same page object when no title is detected.
functions.if_none: No band returns the page unchanged; unchanged code, pinned by a wiring test because its behaviour follows the detector.

values.value: _MARGIN_LABEL_BESIDE_WORD_PT, the distance within which a word counts as beside a glyph
values.if_missing: Not optional: a module constant; the tests pin it by probing 0 and the 40pt rule.

values.value: _MARGIN_LABEL_MAX_BESIDE_FRACTION, the share of glyphs beside a word that makes a run a list
values.if_missing: Not optional: a module constant; the stray-word test fails if it is set so one close word rejects.

values.value: _MARGIN_LABEL_EDGE_FRACTION, how close to a page edge a run must lie to be a title
values.if_missing: Not optional: a module constant; probing 0.5 and 0.02 turns tests red in both directions.

values.value: page words from pdfplumber extract_words() and the page box (page.bbox left edge and width)
values.if_missing: An empty word list returns no band and the page is read unstripped; a page with no usable box falls back to x=0 and page.width, and a page with neither skips the edge check. Wiring tests pin that the box is passed.

queries: N/A - no query added or changed.

break_it.scenario: An Objectives list with seven 'To' bullets 2.4pt apart at one x, as on waverley page 129.
break_it.what_happens: The stack passes the contiguity, length and alphabet checks and every character in that x-band on the page is deleted, including letters of other words.
break_it.how: Every bullet has its own next word 2.5pt beside it, so all glyphs count as beside a word and the run is rejected.

break_it.scenario: A sub-bullet list of twelve 'o' markers whose baseline sits slightly off its item text, as on waverley page 7.
break_it.what_happens: A same-line test by top coordinate finds no neighbour, so the markers look isolated and the band is stripped.
break_it.how: Neighbours are found by vertical overlap, not equal top; each item word overlaps its marker 11.4pt away.

break_it.scenario: The real marrickville title on page 21, where body text reaches within 33-39pt of 6 of its 38 glyphs.
break_it.what_happens: A single 'no word within 40pt' rule rejects the real title and its letters interleave into the rules on that page.
break_it.how: Only a word within 20pt counts, and a run is rejected only when at least half its glyphs have one; measured on all 12 title pages.

break_it.scenario: A page number or callout printed right beside one glyph of a real title.
break_it.what_happens: If one close word were enough to reject, the title would stop being stripped on that page.
break_it.how: One glyph of 38 beside a word is under the half threshold; a test pins it.

break_it.scenario: A list whose markers sit more than 20pt from their text, for example tab-indented markers.
break_it.what_happens: The run would still pass as a title and its band would be stripped, as before this change.
break_it.how: Raised by cross-review on the first push. A run must also lie within 12% of a page edge: every waverley stack sat at 17.8-30.5% of page width, the real marrickville title at 92.6-93.6% on all 12 pages, and text columns start at 12-15%. A list in the text column is never stripped, whatever its marker gap.

break_it.scenario: A PDF page whose box starts at a non-zero x, for example spanning x=100 to 695, with a list stack inside its text column at x=550.
break_it.what_happens: Measured from x=0 the stack sits in the right-hand 12% and is stripped, deleting body letters in its band.
break_it.how: Raised by cross-review on the second push. The edge zone is measured from the page's own box, page.bbox, which _strip_vertical_margin_label passes in; waverley and marrickville page boxes start at x=0, so their measured results are unchanged.

break_it.scenario: A council prints its running title inside the text column, or in a margin wider than 12% of the page.
break_it.what_happens: The title is no longer stripped, so its letters interleave into the rule text on those pages.
break_it.how: Deliberate: an ambiguous stack is left in the text, where review shows garbled lines, instead of being deleted with body letters. Not observed on the two councils measured.

break_it.scenario: Other councils' live and queued rules were extracted with the old strip.
break_it.what_happens: Any page where the old guard misfired may already carry dropped letters or words in served text.
break_it.how: Code cannot repair text already extracted. Not measured beyond waverley and one marrickville chapter; each council needs re-extraction and a line check against its PDFs. Stated in the PR.
break_it.repro: Re-run the line check from the waverley review (words of each line in order on the PDF pages) per council after re-extraction.

post_merge.db_reset: No schema or data change. Waverley is re-queued from merged code in review mode.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: re-queue waverley and re-run the line check; expect only the 98 table-order lines that match plain pdfplumber, then review.
